clues: This town sits on the west side of a saltwater lagoon in Murcia, in the southeast of Spain. It began as a small fishing village.
The lagoon here stays warmer than the big sea next to it. Its warm water draws sailors, windsurfers, and kiteboarders.
This town won the right to rule itself in October nineteen eighty-three. It still marks that week each year with live music and fireworks.
A Hemingway novel turned into a film used this town as a filming place. The Garden of Eden movie was shot here in two thousand eight.
Its lagoon is the largest saltwater lagoon in Europe. Folks call that lagoon the Mar Menor, or the little sea.
